recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR core. Future wording, metadata, or validation-behavior changes for these extension definitions should be made in HL7/fhir-extensions rather than by reintroducing core-owned extension definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-38789 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked to replace the confusing StructureDefinition dependencies extension with two separate extensions: imposeProfile for validator-enforced co-validation and compliesWithProfile for a consistency assertion without the same validation implication.
initial_application: HL7/fhir-extensions commit 460ff82 added StructureDefinition-structuredefinition-imposeProfile.xml and StructureDefinition-structuredefinition-compliesWithProfile.xml with the requested semantics. A later Extension Pack commit, 59c3868, restored the old structuredefinition-dependencies artifact as retired/deprecated with a standards-status reason pointing to structuredefinition-imposeProfile.
additional_context: The Zulip thread named in the Jira explains the difference between invoking another profile during validation and merely asserting consistency. FHIR-I minutes record the 2022-12-12 Persuasive vote. Later Extension Pack issues FHIR-46974 and FHIR-49727 refined wording and title metadata without changing the split. Current core source has no active fhir.ini entry for the old extension definition, but does retain OID assignments and later OperationDefinition guidance that references imposeProfile.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. No FHIR core source edit is warranted because the active extension definitions are maintained in the Extension Pack and the current core checkout has only appropriate references/OID data.

related_jiras.note: Published Extension Pack clarification that refined the compliesWithProfile description after the FHIR-38789 split.
